name: PET (Polyethylene Terephthalate)
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required for specific application
recyclability: Recyclable (PET — widely recyclable stream in India, subject to local infrastructure)
notes: Biaxially oriented PET (BOPET). Commonly used as outer layer in flexible laminates. Good clarity, dimensional stability, oxygen and moisture barrier (moderate). Specific OTR/WVTR values depend on thickness, orientation, and grade — see material_properties. Cost data unavailable in this prototype version.

name: PE (Polyethylene — LDPE/LLDPE)
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required for specific application
recyclability: Recyclable (PE stream — depends on local collection infrastructure)
notes: Low/linear low density polyethylene. Primarily used as sealant layer and inner contact layer. Provides heat-seal capability and good moisture barrier. Relatively high oxygen transmission rate — poor oxygen barrier on its own. Cost data unavailable in this prototype version.

name: BOPP (Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene)
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required for specific application
recyclability: Recyclable (PP stream — less widely available than PET)
notes: Biaxially oriented PP. Good clarity, stiffness, moderate barrier. Widely used for snack food packaging as outer layer. Lower cost than PET in some markets. Cost data unavailable in this prototype version.

name: Metallised PET (MetPET)
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required; metallised layer is typically aluminium, not intended as food-contact surface
recyclability: Difficult to recycle (metallised layers complicate separation)
notes: Aluminium-metallised BOPET. Enhanced oxygen and moisture barrier compared to plain PET. Used as barrier layer in laminates (not food-contact surface). Recycling is more complex than plain PET. MetPET is not equivalent to aluminium foil in barrier performance — typical OTR and WVTR are better than plain film but inferior to solid Al foil. Specific values require validation.

name: Metallised BOPP (MetBOPP)
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required
recyclability: Difficult to recycle (metallised layers complicate separation)
notes: Aluminium-metallised BOPP. Provides enhanced barrier over plain BOPP. Common in Indian snack food laminates as cost-effective barrier layer. Specific OTR/WVTR values vary with metallisation quality and thickness — not reproduced here without validated source.

name: Aluminium Foil (AL)
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required; typically used as non-contact barrier layer
recyclability: Recyclable in principle; lamination makes separation difficult
notes: Solid aluminium foil. Provides near-zero oxygen and moisture transmission when defect-free. Used in PET/AL/PE and similar high-barrier structures. Higher cost and weight; limits recyclability when laminated. Specific minimum thickness for effective barrier performance requires validation — defects, pinholes, and processing affect actual barrier.

name: PP (Polypropylene — cast/blown)
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required
notes: Cast or blown polypropylene. Lower stiffness than BOPP. Used as sealant layer or mono-film for applications requiring moderate barrier. Suitable for MAP applications as a base film with controlled permeability. Specific permeability values depend on grade and thickness.

name: Paper / Kraft Paper
food_contact_standard: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018 — Schedule check required; food-grade paper specifications apply
notes: Food-grade kraft/paper substrate. No inherent moisture or oxygen barrier on its own. Used in Paper/PE laminates to provide stiffness, printability, and sustainability credentials. Food contact compliance depends on paper grade and coatings.
